posts.title: 2025 in reading, watching, listening, etc.
posts.description: No time for intros! Welcome! Usual drill except with no art or theatre sections because I've been to neither since I moved back to Glasgow. Books I read Giovanni's Room at the beginning of February and — to be honest — it feels like that was five years ago. I do remember telling a guy at the end of a (good) date that I was excited to get the bus home because it would give me more time to read this

posts.title: INT. Lumon Industries
posts.description: An innie is born fully clothed, lying on a conference room table, the voice of God (their manager) coming to them from a speaker. The table is pleasantly ovular, the walls padded — perhaps sound-proof, in case they scream and disturb their fellow employees. They wake up with knowledge and without memories, able to name a state but not the colour of their mother's eyes. The world they are born into

posts.title: How perfectionism ruined Star Wars
posts.description: In 1988, George Lucas went with Steven Spielberg to the US Senate and delivered a speech in favour of the rights of artists to protect their work from alteration. Railing against the trend at the time for colourisation of black and white films, he said: Today, engineers with their computers can add colour to black-and-white movies, change the sound track, speed up the pace and add or subtract mate
